HWG § 3a prohibits advertising a medicinal product that requires marketing
authorisation and does not have one. It applies to Arzneimittel only, and the
reference file says so explicitly.

PASS requires:
(1) HWG § 3a is NOT applied to this device.
      - PASS: § 3a is not mentioned, or is mentioned only to exclude it
        ("§ 3a covers Arzneimittel, not devices").
      - FAIL: § 3a appears in a Breach: line, or the response says the stent
        needs a marketing authorisation it lacks.

    is stated to be CE marked with a notified body involved, so on the supplied material
    there is no basis to say it misleads. Any of these pass: `Breach: none`; a provision

    same place. Judge the CONCLUSION and its reasoning, not the format.
    FAIL only if it is asserted as breached with no stated conflict with the supplied
    facts, or if the line is ignored entirely.

    Any sound treatment passes, including reasoning that it reads two ways (as a device
    property under 7(a), curable by data; or as an indication under 7(d), not curable).
    FAIL only if the phrase is not examined at all.

Note for the judge: this skill's output format is a guide, not a checklist. A response
that reaches the right conclusion with sound reasoning in prose passes. Do not fail it
for wording a Breach line differently.

FAIL if § 3a is applied to a device. The drug-eluting framing is the bait.

# Device Claims Review: congress booth panel (19 words)

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-19
**Device:** Sirolimus-eluting coronary stent, Class IIb, CE marked, notified body involved
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Fachkreise (interventional cardiologists at a congress booth), as stated. HWG § 11 therefore does not apply. One caveat below.
**Markets:** DE (EU layer applies throughout)

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. 0 cut, 2 reword, 2 verify, 0 clean as written.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below.

The copy's problem is not accuracy — it is that two of its four assertions are stated without the condition that makes them true. "Approved" is the higher-exposure one, because it misdescribes regulatory status rather than performance, and that is the kind of claim a competitor can assess from the booth panel alone.

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "Approved and available now" — the word *Approved*
**Breach:** UWG § 5(2) no. 4 `[verified]`
**Why:** § 5(2) no. 4 catches "Aussagen oder Symbole, die […] sich auf eine **Zulassung** des Unternehmers oder der Waren oder Dienstleistungen beziehen". "Approved" describes a *Zulassung*; what this device holds, on your own account, is a CE marking following notified-body conformity assessment under MDR. Those are different regulatory statuses, and the copy asserts the one the device does not have.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. The certificate is real; the word for it is wrong. Cured by renaming, not by documenting.
**Also engaged:** HWG § 3 no. 3(a) `[verified]` (zur Täuschung geeignete Angaben über die Beschaffenheit), if the German rendering is "zugelassen" — that word carries the Arzneimittel-authorisation sense more strongly than English "approved" does. Check the German panel, not just this English source text.
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "CE-marked and available now." If you want the notified-body involvement visible, "CE-marked under MDR" is the safe upper bound — do not name or imply a class or certificate scope the certificate does not carry.

*Not cited, deliberately:* HWG § 3a (advertising unauthorised medicinal products) is limited to Arzneimittel and does not reach devices `[verified]`. If anyone in the review chain reaches for it here, that is a false positive.

---

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release across the full lesion"— the phrase *across the full lesion*
**Breach:** MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]`
**Why:** Art. 7(a) prohibits "ascribing functions and properties to the device which the device does not have". A stent elutes drug from the stented segment. Lesion-wide delivery is therefore conditional on the deployed stent length matching the lesion; stated unconditionally, the copy ascribes a coverage property that holds only under a sizing condition the panel does not state. This is the "capability stated without the qualifying condition" shape.
**Evidence needed:** n/a for the unconditional form — evidence of good elution uniformity does not make lesion-wide coverage unconditional. Narrowing the claim cures it.
**Also engaged:**
- MDR Art. 7(d) `[verified]`, if the assessed intended purpose limits lesion length or reference vessel diameter and "full lesion" reads past that range. I cannot close this without the intended purpose.
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a) `[verified]` (Erfolg mit Sicherheit), if the German rendering — e.g. "über die gesamte Läsion" — reads as an assured lesion-wide therapeutic result rather than a statement about where drug is released.
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "sustained drug release across the full stented segment". This keeps the intended point (uniform elution end to end, no cold zones) and drops the implied claim about lesions of arbitrary length.

---

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release" — the phrase *sustained*
**Breach:** none
**Why:** An elution-kinetics claim that is ordinary for the product category and checkable against your own data. Not misleading on the material supplied.
**Evidence needed:** The elution profile from the technical documentation, and the release duration it supports. "Sustained" should be anchored to a stated period if you have one — a named duration is cheap to defend; an open-ended adjective is not.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 `[verified]` ("von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse", "Tests"), if the elution data behind "sustained" is bench-only and the booth context invites it to be read as a clinical durability claim.
**Call:** Verify
**Suggested fix:** If the file supports it: "sustained sirolimus release over [X] days". If it does not, leave "sustained" as is — it is defensible, just less so.

---

**Claim:** "available now"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Availability is an express § 5(2) no. 1 characteristic ("Verfügbarkeit"), but the claim is not misleading on anything I have been shown.
**Evidence needed:** Confirmation that the product is actually shipping in Germany as of the congress date, across the size matrix displayed at the booth.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 4 `[verified]`, if the CE certificate does not cover every diameter/length configuration shown on the stand — "available now" next to a full size chart asserts availability for all of it.
**Call:** Verify

---

### Limb (c) — not raised, and here is why

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I am not converting that into a finding: I have not seen the IFU, and Art. 7(c) turns on a **likely** risk associated with use in line with the intended purpose. Inferring one from "drug-eluting coronary stent" and then flagging the copy for omitting it would be unfalsifiable.

Worth checking against the IFU: whether it records a likely risk or a use condition — particularly any concomitant-therapy requirement — that this panel's benefit-only framing omits. If it does, the proportionate fix for a 19-word trade-show panel is an IFU pointer, not safety text on the board. Congress booth copy for Fachkreise is not expected to carry patient-facing warnings.

### Provisions checked and not engaged

- **HWG § 11 `[verified]`** — applies only outside Fachkreise. Your audience is interventional cardiologists at a congress. One caveat: if the exhibition hall is open to press, patient-advocacy delegates, or the public on any day, the panel is no longer purely Fachkreise-facing and § 11 nos. 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 come into scope. Nothing in the current copy looks like a no. 7 shape, so the practical exposure is low either way — but confirm the hall access rules before assuming § 11 is out.
- **UWG § 6 `[verified]`** — no comparison, express or implied. No comparator is identifiable in the copy, so § 6(1) is not triggered at all.
- **HWG § 3 no. 2(b) `[verified]`** — no absence-of-side-effects claim.

## Revised copy, paste-ready

> Our sirolimus-eluting stent delivers sustained drug release across the full stented segment. CE-marked and available now.

German, if the panel runs in German — have a native reviewer confirm the wording carries the same narrowing:

> Unser Sirolimus-freisetzender Stent bietet eine anhaltende Wirkstofffreisetzung über das gesamte gestentete Segment. CE-gekennzeichnet und ab sofort verfügbar.

Two words carry the fix: **stented segment** in place of "lesion", and **CE-marked** in place of "Approved".

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "sustained" | Elution profile and supportable release duration | R&D / technical documentation owner |
| "CE-marked" | Certificate scope: which configurations it covers | RA / QM |
| "available now" | German shipping status at congress date, all displayed sizes | Commercial / supply chain |
| "full stented segment" | Assessed intended purpose verbatim (lesion length, RVD range) | RA, from the DoC |
| (c) omission | IFU: likely risks and use conditions | RA / clinical affairs |

## Limb (d) — not assessed

Limb (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is **not assessed**: I have not seen the intended purpose. It is the limb device marketing trips most often, so paste it from the technical documentation or DoC and I will cover it. Everything above reviews limbs (a), (b) and (c).

It matters more than usual here. "Full lesion" is exactly the phrase that drifts past a labelled lesion-length or vessel-diameter range, and a limb (d) breach is not cured by data — only by narrowing the claim or extending the conformity assessment.

## Provisions cited

All `[verified]` — verbatim in the skill's reference files, retrieved 2026-09-09:

- MDR Art. 7(a), 7(c), 7(d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md`
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a), § 3 no. 3(a); § 3a and § 11 noted as not applicable — `references/hwg.md`
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1, § 5(2) no. 4; § 6 noted as not engaged — `references/uwg.md`

No source outside these files was used. I have not stated how a German court would treat any of this — the case law that shapes HWG and UWG in practice is outside what this review verifies.

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below.

The copy is short and makes no outcome promise, so § 3 no. 2(a) and 2(b) are clear. The two real problems are "across the full lesion" (unconditional performance claim on something that is anatomy- and sizing-dependent) and "Approved" (a medicinal-products word for a device that holds a CE certificate, not an approval).

## Findings

**Claim:** "across the full lesion"
**Breach:** MDR Art. 7(a); HWG § 3 no. 1; UWG § 5(2) no. 1 `[verified]`
**Why:** Art. 7(a) prohibits "ascribing functions and properties to the device which the device does not have". A stent elutes only where it is deployed; full-lesion drug coverage is conditional on stent length matching lesion length and on the operator avoiding geographic miss. Stated unconditionally, the copy ascribes a property the device has only under a condition the copy omits. § 5(2) no. 1 catches the same thing as "Zwecktauglichkeit" and "von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse".
**Second problem:** the phrase is ambiguous between two different claims — (i) drug reaches the whole treated lesion, and (ii) drug distributes uniformly along the stent without inter-strut gaps. Those need different data. An ambiguous performance claim cannot be substantiated by either dataset.
**Evidence needed:** the release/distribution data supporting whichever claim you mean, plus the stent length matrix.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(d) and UWG § 5(2) no. 4, if "full lesion" reads as suitability for lesion lengths or diffuse disease outside the certificate scope — cannot be resolved without the intended purpose.
**Call:** Needs rewording — narrow to the stented segment, or state the uniformity claim explicitly and carry the data.

**Claim:** "Approved"
**Breach:** UWG § 5(2) no. 4 `[verified]`
**Why:** § 5(2) no. 4 covers "Aussagen oder Symbole, die [...] sich auf eine **Zulassung** des Unternehmers oder der Waren oder Dienstleistungen beziehen". There is no EU approval or Zulassung for a medical device — the device holds a CE marking following conformity assessment with a notified body. "Approved", and still more its German rendering "zugelassen", asserts a regulatory status of a kind the device does not hold, and borrows the weight of the medicinal-product regime. This is a finding independently of whether the performance claims hold.
**Note:** HWG § 3a is **not** cited — it is limited to Arzneimittel and does not apply to devices.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. Cured by naming the actual status.
**Call:** Needs rewording — state "CE-marked under MDR (Class IIb)" and, if you want the credibility, the notified body number.

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release"
**Breach:** none on the material supplied
**Why:** a technical performance claim, not an outcome promise. "Sustained" is undefined but not misleading on its face, and § 3 no. 2(a) (Erfolg mit Sicherheit) is not engaged — the copy promises elution behaviour, not clinical success.
**Evidence needed:** release-kinetics data from the technical file; the elution period in days.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a), HWG § 3 no. 1, UWG § 5(2) no. 1, if the release profile does not support "sustained" as a cardiologist would read it, or if the figure comes from bench data presented as in-vivo performance.
**Call:** Verify — and consider stating the period. A number is cheaper to defend than an adjective.

**Claim:** "available now"
**Breach:** none on the material supplied
**Why:** "Verfügbarkeit" is the first item listed in § 5(2) no. 1, so availability claims are squarely in scope, but nothing in front of me says the claim is untrue.
**Evidence needed:** confirmation that the device is orderable in Germany on the date of the congress, in the sizes shown or implied on the panel.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1, if only part of the size matrix is shipping, or if availability is limited to selected centres or a launch programme.
**Call:** Verify — if partial, qualify it ("initial sizes available now").

## Limb (c): open question, not a finding

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I am not raising an Art. 7(c) finding, because I have not seen the IFU and I will not infer a likely risk from the device category and then flag the copy for omitting it.

> The copy surfaces no limitation. I can't tell from what I have whether the IFU records a likely risk that belongs here. Worth checking against the IFU.

Context cuts in your favour: a congress panel for interventional cardiologists is not expected to carry patient-facing safety text, and where (c) does bite on an asset this short, an IFU pointer is the proportionate fix rather than a risk paragraph. I have included one in the revised copy below. Whether a pointer is sufficient in a given format is shaped by enforcement practice this skill does not verify `[verify]`.

## Checked and clear

- **HWG § 3 no. 2(a)** guaranteed success — no certainty-of-outcome language.
- **HWG § 3 no. 2(b)** no harmful effects — the copy does not claim absence of side effects. Omitting risks is not the same as denying them; that question lives under Art. 7(c) above.
- **HWG § 3 no. 3(b)** claims about the maker — none present.
- **HWG § 11** — Fachkreise, does not apply. If this panel's text or artwork is reused on an ungated web page or in a patient-facing handout, § 11 nos. 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12 come back into scope; no. 7 in particular.
- **UWG § 6** — no comparison, no competitor made erkennbar. If the panel sits beside a comparison chart or the booth staff work from comparative talk tracks, § 6(2) needs its own pass, and no. 2 (nachprüfbar) is where undefined comparators fail.

## Revised copy, paste-ready

English:

> Our sirolimus-eluting stent provides controlled drug release over [X] days across the stented segment. CE-marked under MDR (Class IIb, Notified Body [NNNN]). Available now in Germany. Please consult the Instructions for Use for indications, contraindications and warnings.

German (this is the version HWG and UWG are applied to if the panel is in German):

> Unser Sirolimus-freisetzender Stent gibt den Wirkstoff über [X] Tage kontrolliert über das gestentete Segment ab. CE-gekennzeichnet nach MDR (Klasse IIb, Benannte Stelle [NNNN]). Ab sofort in Deutschland verfügbar. Bitte beachten Sie die Gebrauchsanweisung (Indikationen, Kontraindikationen, Warnhinweise).

Three changes: "full lesion" → "stented segment"; "Approved" → the actual certification status; an IFU pointer. Do not use "zugelassen" anywhere on the panel.

# Device Claims Review: congress booth panel copy

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-19
**Device:** Sirolimus-eluting coronary stent, Class IIb, CE marked, notified body involved
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** **NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed**
**Audience:** Fachkreise (interventional cardiologists, congress booth) — accepted, see note below
**Markets:** DE (EU device rules apply throughout)

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. 0 cut, 2 reword, 2 verify, 0 clean as written.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below.

**Audience note:** Fachkreise is the right call for a booth staffed to cardiologists at a congress, so **HWG § 11 does not apply** and I have not tested against it. One condition: if the same panel is reused on an ungated web page, in a press pack, or on a public/patient day at the venue, the audience flips to Publikum and § 11 nos. 7 and 9 come into play. The panel as drafted would need re-review at that point.

---

## Findings

### 1. "across the full lesion"

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release **across the full lesion**"
**Breach:** MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]`; HWG § 3 no. 1 `[verified]`
**Why:** Art. 7(a) prohibits "ascribing functions and properties to the device which the device does not have". A stent elutes drug from its coated struts — i.e. across the **stented segment**, not across "the lesion". Whether the stented segment equals the full lesion is a function of operator sizing and the available length matrix, not a property of the device. The copy converts a contingent procedural outcome into an inherent device property. HWG § 3 no. 1 is the German mirror ("Wirkungen beigelegt werden, die sie nicht haben").
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. No elution study can make full-lesion coverage a device property; the fix is to describe the segment the device actually covers.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(d) and UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("Zwecktauglichkeit, Verwendungsmöglichkeit") `[verified]` — **if** the assessed intended purpose or the CE-certified size matrix is limited to lesions up to a stated length, "full lesion" also suggests use in long or diffuse lesions the conformity assessment did not cover. I cannot assess this without the intended purpose.
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "delivers controlled sirolimus release across the stented segment"

### 2. "Approved"

**Claim:** "**Approved** and available now."
**Breach:** none on the material supplied — the device is CE marked and a notified body was involved, so there is a real conformity assessment behind the word.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 4 `[verified]` — "Aussagen oder Symbole, die ... sich auf eine **Zulassung** der Waren ... beziehen". Two conditions would make this bite: (i) EU devices are not "approved" under an authorisation regime, they are CE marked following conformity assessment, so a bare "Approved" names no regime, no body and no scope; (ii) read together with sentence 1, "Approved" is capable of being read as approval **for the full-lesion use claimed immediately before it**, which is the scope question in finding 1. The § 5(1) materiality filter cuts the other way for this audience — interventional cardiologists know what CE marking is — but the fix is free, so the exposure is not worth carrying.
**Evidence needed:** the CE certificate and its scope, plus the notified body number.
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "CE marked, Class IIb (Notified Body [NB number])"

### 3. "sustained drug release"

**Claim:** "delivers **sustained** drug release"
**Breach:** none. A controlled-elution claim is ordinary and accurate for a DES; nothing in it conflicts with the operative words of any provision I verify.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse", and "Tests") `[verified]` — **if** the elution kinetics in the technical file do not support "sustained" as a Fachkreise reader would understand it, or if the supporting figure is drawn selectively from bench data. "Sustained" with no duration is vague rather than false, but vague is also the version you cannot defend cheaply in an Abmahnung.
**Evidence needed:** in-vitro/in-vivo elution profile from the technical documentation; the release duration you can stand behind.
**Call:** Verify — and consider naming the number. "Controlled release over [X] days" is both stronger to this audience and easier to defend than "sustained".

### 4. "available now"

**Claim:** "**available now**"
**Breach:** none on the material supplied.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 `[verified]` — "Verfügbarkeit" is an express item in the statute. If the stent is not actually orderable in Germany at the time of the congress, or if only part of the diameter/length matrix is shipping while the panel implies the whole range, that is a § 5 finding independent of every performance claim.
**Evidence needed:** DE commercial availability date and the size matrix actually released.
**Call:** Verify

---

## Open question: limb (c)

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I am **not** raising an Art. 7(c) finding, because I have not seen the IFU and I will not infer a likely risk from the device category and then flag the copy for omitting it. That said, a drug-eluting stent IFU will carry contraindications and concomitant-therapy requirements, and this is the limb worth checking deliberately:

> Check the panel against the IFU's contraindications and warnings. If there is a likely risk associated with use in line with the intended purpose, a booth panel is not expected to reproduce it in full — the proportionate fix for trade-show copy is an IFU pointer, not patient-facing safety text.

---

## Paste-ready revised copy

Fill the bracketed slots from the technical file and the CE certificate:

> **Sirolimus-eluting coronary stent**

The copy is 20 words and carries two structural problems: a delivery claim whose scope is the *lesion* when the device's property is confined to the *stented segment*, and "Approved", which for a CE-marked device asserts a regulatory status that does not exist in that form.

**Claim:** "across the full lesion"
**Breach:** MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]`; HWG § 3 no. 1 `[verified]`
**Why:** Art. 7(a) prohibits "ascribing functions and properties to the device which the device does not have". A drug-eluting stent elutes from its coated surface into the adjacent vessel wall — its delivery property is bounded by the stented segment, not by the lesion. Whether the lesion is fully covered depends on operator sizing and placement, not on the device. Stated unconditionally, the copy ascribes to the device a coverage property that is contingent on a user variable. HWG § 3 no. 1 is the same test in German form ("Wirkungen beigelegt werden, die sie nicht haben").
**Evidence needed:** n/a on the face of it — this is a scope-of-claim defect, not a data gap. If the technical documentation *does* express the elution performance in lesion terms (e.g. a validated full-lesion-coverage claim tied to a sizing matrix), send it and I will re-review; that would change the analysis.

**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "sustained drug release across the stented segment"

---

**Claim:** "Approved"
**Breach:** UWG § 5(2) no. 4 `[verified]`
**Why:** § 5(2) no. 4 covers "Aussagen oder Symbole, die [...] sich auf eine **Zulassung** des Unternehmers oder der Waren oder Dienstleistungen beziehen". A Class IIb device carries a CE marking on the basis of a notified body certificate — it is not "approved"/"zugelassen" by an authority. To a German-market audience "Approved" maps onto *Zulassung*, a status this device does not hold, and it is capable of influencing a purchasing decision (§ 5(1) materiality is met at a procurement-facing booth). The accurate status is also the stronger one: the NB number is a concrete, checkable credential that "Approved" throws away.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. Cured by stating the actual status.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 3 (Status of the *trader*) if booth material elsewhere attributes the approval to the company rather than the goods. Note: **HWG § 3a does not apply** — it is limited to Arzneimittel, and citing it against a device is a false positive.
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "CE marked (Class IIb, notified body [NB number])"

---

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** A sustained-release profile is an ordinary, substantiable property of a DES and the claim is not misleading on the material supplied. But "sustained" is undefined, and the elution profile in the technical file will have a specific duration and curve.

**Call:** Verify

**Why:** Availability is an essential characteristic under UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("wesentlichen Merkmale der Ware wie **Verfügbarkeit**"). Not misleading on what I have, but it rests on a fact I cannot see.
**Evidence needed:** Confirm the device is orderable in Germany on the review date, and that the certificate scope plus actual stock cover the **full** size/diameter matrix a cardiologist would infer from an unqualified "available now". If only part of the range ships, qualify it.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1, if availability is limited to selected sizes, a pilot/limited market release, or markets other than DE.
**Call:** Verify

## Regulatory review — DES booth copy, DE / Fachkreise

Two of the eleven words carry most of the risk. Short version: **don't run this as written.**

### Blocking issues

**1. "Approved" — misleading, MDR Art. 7 + §3 HWG**
Medical devices in the EU are not "approved." They are CE marked following a conformity assessment. The German equivalent, *"zugelassen,"* is a term of art for medicinal products (marketing authorisation) and German courts and competitors treat it as *irreführend* when applied to a device — it suggests a state authority reviewed and endorsed the product. Replace with a CE-marking statement naming the regulation and the notified body's identification number. Do not phrase the notified body's involvement as endorsement or certification of quality.

**2. "across the full lesion" — implies uses beyond the intended purpose, MDR Art. 7(a)/(d)**
This reads as uniform drug distribution over the entire lesion regardless of lesion length, morphology or vessel diameter. Your intended purpose almost certainly carries limits (vessel Ø range, max lesion length, exclusions such as left main, bifurcations, in-stent restenosis). A claim that outruns the IFU is the classic MDR Art. 7 finding and the easiest one for a competitor to attack under §3 HWG / §5 UWG. Either qualify with the actual indicated ranges or drop the phrase.

**3. "sustained drug release" — unsubstantiated performance claim**
"Sustained" is meaningless without a duration, a test model, and a source. Needs: release period in days, whether the data are in vitro, preclinical or clinical, and a pointer to data on file / the clinical evaluation report. Hold the substantiation in a claims matrix cross-referenced to the CER and IFU before the congress, not after.

**4. No risk information and no IFU reference — MDR Art. 7(c)**
Creating a false impression by omitting likely risk is explicitly prohibited. Add an IFU reference covering intended purpose, contraindications, warnings and precautions. Important: do **not** use *"Zu Risiken und Nebenwirkungen…"* — that is §4 Abs. 3 HWG drug wording and would itself be misleading on a device.

### Check before print

- **Classification looks wrong.** A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent is an implantable device in direct contact with the central circulatory system *and* incorporates a medicinal substance with ancillary action — MDR Annex VIII Rules 8 and 14 both push it to **Class III**, not IIb. This isn't cosmetic: Class III brings the medicinal-substance consultation procedure and a different evidence bar for exactly the claims above. Verify against the certificate before anything else; if the certificate really says IIb, that is a conversation with your notified body, not a copy edit.
- **"available now"** must be true in Germany, for the configurations shown, on the day the panel is up. Qualify if you're in limited market release or if some sizes aren't yet CE-covered.
- **Fachkreise status of the booth.** The Fachkreise exemption only holds if access is genuinely restricted. Open halls, lay press or patient-advocacy attendees pull you into §11 HWG territory.
- **Language.** MPDG permits English labelling/IFU for devices supplied exclusively to professional users under certain conditions — confirm your product falls in scope, otherwise German IFU is required for the German market. Booth copy itself can be English for Fachkreise.
- **Booth conduct** under the MedTech Europe Code and BVMed Kodex Medizinprodukte (hospitality, giveaways, HCP interactions) — separate workstream, worth confirming it's covered.
- Add material code, version and approval date to the artwork.

### Revised copy

**EN**
> Sirolimus-eluting coronary stent system. Controlled sirolimus release over [X] days ([in vitro / preclinical] data on file). For vessel diameters [x–y] mm and lesion lengths up to [z] mm, in line with the intended purpose. CE marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745; notified body [name, ID no.]. Available in Germany. For healthcare professionals only. Please consult the Instructions for Use for the full intended purpose, contraindications, warnings and precautions.

**DE**
> Sirolimus-freisetzendes Koronarstentsystem. Kontrollierte Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [X] Tage ([In-vitro-/präklinische] Daten auf Anfrage). Für Gefäßdurchmesser [x–y] mm und Läsionslängen bis [z] mm gemäß Zweckbestimmung. CE-Kennzeichnung gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745, Benannte Stelle [Name, Kenn-Nr.]. In Deutschland verfügbar. In Germany this is the single biggest exposure. A CE-marked device is **konformitätsbewertet**, not **zugelassen**. "Approved" translates to "zugelassen," which German cardiologists read as an *Arzneimittelzulassung* (BfArM/EMA marketing authorisation) — a regulatory status this stent does not have and cannot have. That creates a false impression of the device's regulatory standing under **MDR Art. 7(b)**, and is misleading under **HWG §3** and **UWG §5 Abs. 1**.

Compounding it: your brief mentions a notified body. Do **not** let "approved" become an implied NB endorsement. The NB number exists to accompany the CE mark, not to function as a quality seal or testimonial.

**Fix:** "CE marked" / "CE-gekennzeichnet." Nothing more.

### 🔴 Blocker 2: "across the full lesion"

An unqualified absolute performance claim. It asserts complete drug distribution over the entire lesion as a property of the device, independent of operator technique — which ignores sizing, geographic miss, and edge effects. Two problems:

- **MDR Art. 7(a)/(d)**: it ascribes a property the device may not have, and likely overshoots the intended purpose the conformity assessment actually covered.
- **Substantiation**: if this isn't a verbatim performance claim from your technical documentation with elution/PK data behind it, it fails. "Sustained" needs a number — over how many days?

Check the exact wording in the IFU and the CE technical file. If "full lesion coverage" isn't in there, it can't be on the panel.

---

### 🟠 Should fix before the booth opens

**No risk information, no IFU pointer.** MDR Art. 7(c) prohibits failing to inform the user of likely risks associated with intended use. For an implantable coronary device carrying an antiproliferative agent, promotional copy with zero risk signal is thin. Add the standard referral line.

**No Fachkreise designation.** The Fachkreise route (HWG §2) is what exempts you from the §11 Publikumswerbung restrictions — but only if the audience is actually restricted. Congress booths are frequently walked by press, industry, and accompanying non-HCPs. Mark the material "Nur für Fachkreise," and make sure booth access and any QR-code destination are genuinely gated. If this copy also runs on a website, it needs a gate there too.

**Language.** Anything functioning as labelling must be German (MDR Art. 10(11), MPDG §8). Advertising itself has more latitude at an international congress, but for a German-market panel, German is the safe default — and it forces you to confront the *zugelassen* trap explicitly rather than leaving it to a translator.

**"Available now."** Purely factual, so just make it true on day one — and qualify it if only part of the diameter/length matrix has actually shipped.

---

### ⚠️ Separate issue: the classification in your brief looks wrong

You've stated Class IIb. A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent should be **Class III** under MDR Annex VIII on two independent grounds:

- **Rule 8** — implantable, and the Annex VIII definition of "central circulatory system" explicitly names the *arteriae coronariae*, which pushes it from IIb to III.
- **Rule 14** — a device incorporating an ancillary medicinal substance is Class III regardless.

This is probably just an error in the brief. But if "Class IIb" appears anywhere on the CE certificate, the DoC, or the booth materials, resolve it with RA before the congress — it's a bigger problem than the copy.

---

### Suggested rewrite

**DE (primary):**
> Sirolimus-freisetzender Koronarstent mit kontrollierter Wirkstofffreisetzung über [X] Tage.
> CE-gekennzeichnet. Ab sofort in Deutschland verfügbar.
>
> Nur für Fachkreise. Bitte beachten Sie die Gebrauchsanweisung mit Indikationen, Kontraindikationen, Warnhinweisen und Vorsichtsmaßnahmen.

**EN (if a bilingual panel is wanted):**

> CE marked. Now available in Germany.
>
> For healthcare professionals only. Refer to the Instructions for Use for indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions.

Fill `[X]` from the elution data in the technical file. If your team wants to keep a lesion-coverage message, it needs to be reframed as what the data supports — e.g. drug distribution across the stented segment — and cited to the specific study, not asserted as a device property.

## Biggest flag first: the class is almost certainly wrong

You've described it as **Class IIb**. Under MDR (EU) 2017/745 a sirolimus-eluting coronary stent is **Class III**, on two independent grounds:

- **Annex VIII, Rule 8** — implantable/long-term surgically invasive devices are IIb *unless* intended for direct contact with the heart or central circulatory system. The MDR's definition of "central circulatory system" explicitly names *arteriae coronariae*. → III.
- **Annex VIII, Rule 14** — a device incorporating, as an integral part, a substance that would be a medicinal product on its own and acts with ancillary action. Sirolimus qualifies. → III.

This isn't a copy nit. It changes the conformity route (Annex IX incl. the Section 5.2 medicinal-substance consultation with a competent authority or EMA), the evidence bar for every performance claim below, and possibly your notified body's scope. **Verify the certificate before this copy goes anywhere.** If the certificate genuinely says IIb, that's a bigger conversation than a booth panel.

---

## The copy, line by line

> "Our sirolimus-eluting stent delivers sustained drug release across the full lesion."

**"across the full lesion" — MDR Art. 7(a) and 7(d) risk.** Full lesion coverage is an operator/procedural outcome (geographic miss is a sizing and technique problem), not a device property. As written it ascribes a property the device doesn't have, and it implies performance irrespective of lesion length — potentially beyond the labelled lesion-length range and available stent lengths in your matrix. Bind the claim to the device: *"across the stented segment."*

**"sustained" is unquantified.** It needs a number traceable to your CER/elution data ("over ~90 days", or whatever the release kinetics actually show), and it has to match the intended purpose in the IFU. An unsubstantiated durability claim is the classic § 3 HWG / § 5 UWG target, and competitor *Abmahnung* is a live risk at a German congress.

**No risk information at all.** MDR Art. 7(c) prohibits failing to inform of a likely risk associated with intended use. For a DES that means at minimum a pointer to DAPT requirements, stent thrombosis, and contraindications. The standard mitigation is an IFU reference line — currently absent.

> "Approved and available now."

**"Approved" is the most legally exposed word here.** A CE mark is a conformity assessment, not an authority approval. In German, *"zugelassen"* is a medicinal-products term (AMG) and using it for a device creates a false impression of regulatory status — squarely § 3 HWG (irreführende Werbung) and MDR Art. 7. Say **"CE-marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745."**

---

## Suggested rewrite

**English (Fachkreise):**

> **[Brand] sirolimus-eluting coronary stent system.** Sustained sirolimus release over [X] days across the stented segment.[¹] CE-marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and available in Germany.
>
> For the complete intended purpose, indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions, please refer to the Instructions for Use. For healthcare professionals only.
>
> ¹ [Data source — CER section / pivotal trial citation]

**German:**

> **[Marke] Sirolimus-freisetzendes Koronarstentsystem.** Anhaltende Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [X] Tage im gestenteten Segment.[¹] CE-Kennzeichnung gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745, in Deutschland verfügbar.

## Verdict: Do not run as written. Two claims need rework, and the classification in the brief looks wrong.

---

### 1. "Approved" — highest risk

In the EU there is no "approval" for medical devices. Devices undergo a **conformity assessment** and carry a **CE mark**; only medicinal products are *approved / zugelassen*. This matters more than usual here because the product is a **drug**-eluting stent — a reader could reasonably take "approved" as referring to the sirolimus component having a drug authorisation, which it does not (it's an ancillary medicinal substance assessed via the competent-authority/EMA consultation route, not authorised as a medicine).

- **MDR (EU) 2017/745 Art. 7** — prohibits text, names or symbols that mislead the user as to the device's intended purpose, safety or performance, *including by ascribing functions or properties the device does not have*.
- **HWG § 3** — irreführende Werbung; applies to medical devices and applies to Fachkreise audiences too (the §§ 10–11 Publikumswerbung restrictions are what drop away for HCPs, not § 3).
- **UWG §§ 3, 5** — this is the route a competitor actually uses against you at a German congress. Abmahnung risk is real and fast.

**Fix:** state the regulatory status precisely — "CE marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, Notified Body [4-digit number]."

### 2. "Across the full lesion" — overclaim and possible off-label promotion

"Full lesion" is an absolute claim about a clinical outcome that depends on the operator's sizing, not on the device. It implies the stent covers any lesion completely, which is false for lesions longer than your longest available device and invites use in overlap or long-lesion settings that may not be in your CE-marked intended purpose. Elution is delivered across the **stented segment**, not "the lesion."

Any claim that goes beyond the IFU's intended purpose is off-label promotion and breaches MDR Art. 7 independently of whether it's literally true.

**Fix:** "across the stented segment," with the available length range stated.

### 3. "Sustained drug release" — substantiable, but currently unsubstantiated

Acceptable in principle, but it's a performance claim and needs a defined, referenced release profile consistent with your technical documentation and clinical evaluation. "Sustained" with no number, no timeframe and no citation is exactly what gets challenged.

**Fix:** quantify and cite — e.g. "controlled sirolimus release over [X] days¹" with the footnote pointing to a study or "data on file," and the source physically available at the booth.

### 4. "Available now" — verify, don't assume

Factually checkable and fine *if* the device is actually orderable in Germany on the day of the congress. If launch is staged, or it's CE marked but not yet supplied in DE, this is misleading. Confirm with commercial before print.

### 5. Classification in the brief looks incorrect

You've specified **Class IIb**. A drug-eluting coronary stent should fall under **Class III** — Rule 14 (device incorporating, as an integral part, a substance which if used separately would be a medicinal product) and Rule 8 (implantable device in contact with the central circulatory system) both point to III. Worth confirming against the certificate before anything referencing class or conformity route goes to print, since it changes the NB procedure and the consultation obligation for the sirolimus.

---

## Missing mandatory / expected elements

| Element | Status |
|---|---|
| Full device/brand name and manufacturer | Missing |
| CE mark + Notified Body number | Missing |
| IFU reference | Missing |
| "Nur für Fachkreise" designation | Missing |
| Substantiation footnote for the release claim | Missing |

On language: English is defensible for a Fachkreise congress audience, but the IFU and labelling must be German.

---

## Suggested rewrite

> **[Brand Name] Sirolimus-Eluting Coronary Stent System**
>
> Controlled sirolimus release over [X] days across the stented segment.¹ Available in lengths [A–B] mm.
>
> CE marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 · Notified Body [XXXX] · Now available in Germany.
>
> ¹ [Study / data on file reference]
>
> Nur für Fachkreise. Please refer to the Instructions for Use for the full intended purpose, indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions.

Before sign-off, have someone reconcile every word of the panel against the intended-purpose wording in the CE certificate and IFU — that reconciliation, documented, is your defence if a competitor challenges the booth.

---

## Blockers

**1. "Class IIb" is almost certainly wrong — check this first**

A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent should be **Class III** under MDR (EU) 2017/745, on two independent grounds:
- Rule 8 — implantable in direct contact with the central circulatory system
- Rule 14 — incorporates a medicinal substance with ancillary action

That changes the conformity route (Annex IX with mandatory consultation of a medicinal-product competent authority or EMA on the sirolimus component) and the notified body's scrutiny obligations. If your internal record says IIb, either the record is wrong or something about the device isn't what I've assumed. Resolve before anything goes to print, because everything downstream — what you may claim, what the NB signed off on — hangs off it.

**2. "Approved"**

MDR devices are not approved. They are CE marked following conformity assessment. In German, "zugelassen" invites the reading that a state authority granted a marketing authorisation the way BfArM/EMA does for medicinal products — and that reading has been treated as misleading (§3 HWG, §5 UWG, MDR Art. 7). Fachkreise are less likely to be actually misled than laypeople, but this is a standard Wettbewerbszentrale target and the fix is free.

Geographic miss is a well-documented failure mode, and a stent cannot deliver drug to tissue it doesn't span. Bare "sustained" with no comparator is weak; "sustained" with an implied comparator drags you into §6 UWG comparative-advertising territory, which needs head-to-head data.

- **Booth access.** HWG applies to medical devices via §1(1) Nr. 1a. The §11 restrictions on lay advertising fall away only if the audience really is Fachkreise. - **Language.** If you run English at an international congress, fine, but the German version must be substantiated independently — don't let "approved" become "zugelassen" in translation.

## Suggested rewrite

**German**

> **[Markenname] — Sirolimus-freisetzender Koronarstent**
> Kontrollierte Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [X] Tage, gleichmäßig über die gesamte Stentlänge ([in vitro/in vivo], [Referenz]).
> CE-gekennzeichnet nach Verordnung (EU) 2017/745, Benannte Stelle [NNNN].
> In Deutschland verfügbar: Ø [X–Y] mm, Länge [A–B] mm.
> Zweckbestimmung und Gebrauchsanweisung beachten. Nur für Fachkreise.
> [Hersteller, Anschrift]

**English**

> Controlled sirolimus release over [X] days, uniform across the full stent length ([method], [reference]).
> CE marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, notified body [NNNN].
> Available in Germany: Ø [X–Y] mm, lengths [A–B] mm.
> Refer to the intended purpose and instructions for use. For healthcare professionals only.

1. Classification and conformity route (see blocker 1), plus MDR vs. legacy MDD status
2. Elution duration and uniformity data in the clinical evaluation report / technical documentation, with the exact reference you'll cite
3. Every claim within the IFU intended purpose — nothing beyond it
4. Actual German availability by size

## Verdict

Don't run this as written. Two of the four claims are likely unlawful in Germany, and one is a terminology error that regulators and competitors both watch for. (Not legal advice — route the final version through your regulatory/legal function.)

---

## Issue 1 — "Approved" ❌ Highest risk

In the EU there is no "approval" for medical devices. A Class IIb device undergoes **conformity assessment** with notified body involvement and carries a **CE mark**. Saying "approved" (German: *zugelassen*) borrows the vocabulary of medicinal-product authorisation and implies a state/agency endorsement that does not exist.

- **MDR Art. 7** expressly prohibits text that creates a false impression regarding *certification* or misleads about the device's status.
- The false-approval framing is the classic **§ 3 HWG** (irreführende Werbung) and **§ 5 UWG** fact pattern, and it's a favourite target for *Abmahnung* by competitors and the Wettbewerbszentrale.
- Related: do **not** name or logo the notified body as a quality endorsement. The four-digit NB number may appear only adjacent to the CE mark, not as a selling point.

**Fix:** "CE-marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745" / "CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745".

## Issue 2 — "across the full lesion" ❌ High risk

An absolute coverage claim. Drug release is a property of the stent's own length and coating, not of the lesion. Whether the lesion is fully covered depends on operator sizing, and geographic miss is a known real-world failure mode — so the claim attributes a function the device does not have (**MDR Art. 7(a)**; **§ 3 Nr. 1 HWG**, Wirkungen, die es nicht hat).

**Fix:** anchor to the device, not the anatomy: "across the full stent length" / "über die gesamte Stentlänge", or "across the treated segment".

## Issue 3 — "sustained drug release" ⚠️ Substantiate or qualify

Legitimate in principle, but unquantified. **MDR Art. 7** plus Annex XIV require claims to be supported by clinical evidence, and the claim must not exceed the intended purpose stated in the IFU. Add the release duration with its data source (elution kinetics / pharmacokinetic data, and say whether bench or clinical).

**Fix:** "Sustained sirolimus release over [X] days ([study / data on file])."

## Issue 4 — "available now" ⚠️ Verify

Fine if literally true *in Germany on the congress date* — stock, German-language IFU per MDR Annex I 23.1(f), EUDAMED/DMIDS registration, and an order path. If it's a pre-launch teaser, drop it or say "launching [month]".

## Also check before the booth opens

- **Fachkreise gating.** § 11 HWG (Publikumswerbung) does not apply to *Fachkreise* per § 2 HWG, but that protection depends on the booth actually being restricted — badge control, no public/press-open hours, and the same copy not reused on an open website. If it leaks to laypersons, the whole piece is judged under § 11.
- **Ancillary medicinal substance.** Sirolimus is an ancillary substance under MDR Art. 1(8) / Annex VIII Rule 14. Name it as a device characteristic; don't build the copy around pharmacological efficacy as if promoting a medicine.
- **IFU cross-reference.** Standard and expected: intended purpose, indications, contraindications, warnings.
- **Comparatives.** Nothing comparative here — keep it that way unless you have head-to-head data (§ 6 UWG).

---

## Rewritten copy

**English**

> **[Brand] sirolimus-eluting coronary stent system**
> Sustained sirolimus release over [X] days across the full stent length.¹
> CE-marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745. Available in Germany now.
>
> ¹ [Study / data on file, ref.]. For healthcare professionals only. Please consult the Instructions for Use for the full intended purpose, indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions.

**German**

> **[Marke] Sirolimus-freisetzendes Koronarstentsystem**
> Anhaltende Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [X] Tage über die gesamte Stentlänge.¹
> CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745. Ab sofort in Deutschland verfügbar.
>
> ¹ [Studie / Daten auf Anfrage, Ref.]. Nur für Fachkreise. Bitte beachten Sie die Gebrauchsanweisung mit Zweckbestimmung, Indikationen, Kontraindikationen, Warnhinweisen und Vorsichtsmaßnahmen.

## Verdict: don't run as-is

Two blockers ("Approved", "across the full lesion") and one factual premise that needs checking before anything else.

---

### 0. Check the classification first — "Class IIb" looks wrong

A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent is very likely **Class III**, not IIb, under MDR Annex VIII:

- **Rule 8** — implantables in contact with the *central circulatory system* are Class III, and `arteriae coronariae` are named in the MDR Art. 2 definition of central circulatory system.
- **Rule 14** — devices incorporating a medicinal substance with ancillary action (sirolimus) are Class III, and trigger the Annex IX §5.2 medicinal-substance consultation with a medicines competent authority.

This matters for the copy because Class III implantables carry obligations you'd normally reflect in HCP material: an **SSCP** (Summary of Safety and Clinical Performance) you can cite, and an Implant Card. If the brief genuinely says IIb, that's worth resolving with RA before the booth, not after.

---

### 1. "Approved and available now" — Blocker

**"Approved"** is the single highest-risk word here. Devices are not approved or *zugelassen*; they undergo conformity assessment and carry a CE mark. In Germany, calling a device "zugelassen" is treated as misleading under **§3 HWG** (and **§14 MPDG** / **§3a, §5 UWG**) because it borrows the authority-approval connotation of a medicinal product *Zulassung*. It's also textbook Abmahnung bait from competitors and the Wettbewerbszentrale — cheap for them to send, expensive for you at a congress.

→ Use "CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745" plus the **notified body name and four-digit number**.

**"Available now"** must be literally true on the day, in Germany, for the exhibiting legal entity: device on the market, UDI/EUDAMED in order, and the full size matrix actually shippable. If only part of the matrix has launched, "available now" is misleading by omission (§5a UWG). Say "available in Germany from [date]" or name the available sizes.

### 2. "Across the full lesion" — Blocker

Two independent problems:

- **Scope creep beyond the intended purpose.** "Full lesion" reads as *any* lesion, which invites use outside the labelled vessel-diameter and lesion-length range — squarely **MDR Art. 7(d)** (suggesting uses other than those stated in the conformity assessment). Long/diffuse lesions and bifurcations are exactly where cardiologists will take that reading.
- **Unsubstantiated uniformity claim.** It implies homogeneous drug distribution end to end, i.e. no geographic miss. That needs coating-uniformity and elution data, and it needs the limits stated.

→ Bound it to the label: "for vessels Ø [x–y] mm and lesion lengths up to [z] mm per the IFU."

### 3. "Sustained drug release" — Major

Not wrong, but vague and therefore unsubstantiable as written. **MDR Art. 7(a)** and **§3 HWG** both require claims be backed by the technical documentation. Quantify it and cite the source: "controlled sirolimus release over [N] days ([in-vitro elution / preclinical PK], Ref. [X])."

Also watch the implicit leap HCPs will make from drug kinetics to clinical outcome (late lumen loss, TLR). If you want the outcome benefit, claim it explicitly and cite the trial. If you don't cite it, don't imply it.

### 4. Missing risk information — Major

**MDR Art. 7(c)** prohibits creating a misleading impression by *failing to inform of likely risks*. The copy is all-benefit, zero-balance. Minimum: "Please consult the Instructions for Use for indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions." For a DES, DAPT requirements are the kind of thing HCPs expect to see referenced.

### 5. Fachkreise restriction not stated — Minor but easy

Mark it "Nur für medizinische Fachkreise." Congress booths are more porous than people assume — press, industry guests, patient advocates. If lay-accessible, **§11 HWG** restrictions come into play and the "approved" phrasing gets worse, not better.

### 6. Language — Minor, confirm

Promotional material for the German market in German is the safe default. Labelling and IFU language is governed by **MPDG §8**, which has a professional-use carve-out worth confirming with RA rather than assuming — and it governs the IFU, not your booth panel.

---

## Suggested rewrite

**German (Fachkreise):**

> **[Marke] Sirolimus-freisetzender Koronarstent**
> Kontrollierte Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [N] Tage aus [Polymer-/Trägersystem] ([Datenquelle, Ref. X]).
> Indiziert für [Zweckbestimmung gemäß Gebrauchsanweisung]; Gefäßdurchmesser [x–y] mm, Läsionslänge bis [z] mm.
> CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745, Benannte Stelle [Name, 0123]. In Deutschland verfügbar ab [Datum].
> *Nur für medizinische Fachkreise. Bitte beachten Sie die Gebrauchsanweisung für Indikationen, Kontraindikationen, Warnhinweise und Vorsichtsmaßnahmen.*
> [Hersteller, Anschrift] · [Materialnummer, Stand: MM/JJJJ]

**English mirror:**

> **[Brand] sirolimus-eluting coronary stent**
> Controlled sirolimus release over [N] days from [coating system] ([data source, Ref. X]).
> Indicated for [intended purpose per IFU]; vessel Ø [x–y] mm, lesion length up to [z] mm.
> CE marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, Notified Body [name, 0123]. Available in Germany from [date].
> *For healthcare professionals only. Consult the IFU for indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions.*

---

## Before sign-off

1. Resolve the IIb vs. III classification; if III, cite the SSCP.
2. Build a claims-substantiation matrix: every claim → IFU section or study reference. This is what defends you in an Abmahnung and what an NB asks for.
3. Confirm launch date and the shippable size matrix against "available."
4. Add manufacturer legal entity, material number, and version date.
5. Separately, check booth conduct (hospitality, giveaways) against **§7 HWG** and the MedTech Europe / BVMed codes — out of scope for this copy but same event.

One caveat: this is a regulatory-affairs read, not legal advice. Items 1–3 above need RA/legal sign-off before the congress.
